I will keep my land mainly in the wheat-maize system, because that is what fits my fields, my well irrigation, and the way I have farmed for many years. I am already old, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will not make the work too complicated. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton because I still know that crop well and it gives me another source of income. I will use better seed on all three crops because I care about steady yield more than saving a little money on seed. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too low because I have irrigation and want yield, and not too high because that wastes money. For wheat I will irrigate a couple of times and manage weeds and disease in a simple way. For maize I will sow right after wheat harvest, keep tillage light to save labor and time, and use hybrid seed for stable output. For cotton I will manage it a bit more carefully because it needs more field watching and more spraying than grain crops, but I will only keep a smaller area so it stays within what I can handle. My aim is stable production, manageable labor, and reliable cash income, not taking big risks.
